questions.question: Given that mutual information is just an undirected correlation, why is it introduced as a tool for tracking information flow in circuits?

passages.quote: It does not, however, quantify information transfer between the neurons, as it is an undirected measure that describes the instantaneous dependency between two variables and has no notion of the time-directed structure that we intuitively understand as “transfer” or “flow.”

questions.question: If there is no single agreed way to define redundant information, how can partial information decomposition give a definite answer at all?

passages.quote: Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these, and so considerable work has been devoted to developing formal measures of each.
To date, no single universally accepted measure has been proposed. All measures have their own trade-offs and drawbacks

questions.question: Since most of the studies described rely on the Imin measure that has been criticized as unintuitive, how much should we trust their synergy findings?

passages.quote: The majority of the studies discussed in this paper used the original Imin measure proposed in [1], although this measure has been criticized for unintuitive behavior [29,39].

questions.question: Why does synergy rise with input correlation only up to a point and then fall, instead of just increasing with more shared information?

passages.quote: the synergy began to decrease (this level is marked by the vertical dotted line in Figure 4E).
This suggests that as the similarity of the converging information grows past some point, it becomes redundant, and the total amount of synergistic output is suppressed.

questions.question: If the effective networks were built using bivariate transfer entropy, which is known to overestimate connection significance, how solid are the triad-based synergy conclusions?

passages.quote: it has been shown that bivariate analyses overestimate the significance of bivariate edges [51].

questions.question: Since the cortical culture findings come from in vitro tissue, do they still hold when neurons face real task demands in a behaving animal?

passages.quote: the demands placed on a circuit in the context of a behaving animal are certain to differ from those placed on cultures in vitro.
This increase in relative redundancy was interpreted as a response to the practical requirements of the task

questions.question: Even if synergy reliably marks certain neurons, does finding it actually explain why those neurons process information that way biologically?

passages.quote: it does not necessarily provide a mechanistic explanation for why particular neurons are synergy-dominated or redundancy-dominated.

questions.question: If the number of information atoms explodes combinatorially with more parent neurons, can PID ever describe a real neuron with many inputs?

passages.quote: in the case of six parent neurons, there are 7,828,354 distinct PI atoms, the vast majority of which are difficult to interpret.
Given that single neurons can receive inputs from very large numbers of upstream neurons, a “complete” description of the information dynamics of any individual neuron is completely intractable.

questions.question: Given that finite datasets systematically bias entropy and mutual information estimates upward, could reported synergy values be partly an artifact rather than real computation?

passages.quote: the plug-in estimator for the Shannon entropy consistently underestimates the true entropy and overestimates the mutual information (for example, two processes that are uncorrelated can have non-zero apparent mutual information)
